value.rationale: The finite square Fourier transform on a two-digit Cantor approximation is a natural sampling matrix, and its determinant is its intrinsic basis-volume invariant. The exact complete digit-step optimum quantifies an arithmetically sharp even/odd quotient dichotomy beyond existence of compatible Hadamard digits, with an immediate conditioning implication restricted to that family.

final_claim: For every b>=3, 1<=d<b and depth n>=1 the normalized 2^n-square Fourier matrix with two spatial digits and integer steps t_j in 1..b-1 has determinant magnitude product_j |sin(pi d t_j/b)|^(2^(n-1)), exactly optimized at s_q^(n 2^(n-1)) where q=b/gcd(b,d), s_q=1 if q is even and cos(pi/(2q)) if odd; maximizers have the declared residue congruences, giving unitarity iff q even and the sharp derived bound A_n<=s_q^n if q odd.
limitations: Only 2-digit finite atomic Cantor grid, full square 2^n integer digit-tower frequencies; no arbitrary frequency frame claims or sharp condition-number minimum.
